goal-r1-f1.rationale: T7's threshold-override clause is already binary in the existing acceptance — the verb 'honoured' summarises the binary check that follows: the iteration log's `converged` line records the per-pixel diff value as a number against the configured threshold. A fresh agent runs the override case by setting `admin/config.json.design.diffThreshold = 0.03`, running the skill, and reading the converged-line diff value: pass if `< 0.03`, fail otherwise. The reviewer's proposed sharpened clause ('a run that converges at 0.04 with the override set is a failed run') restates the same binary check but more verbosely. Cited evidence: T7 acceptance line at features/001-design-skill/001-design-skill-tasks.md (Acceptance line 2) — 'records each iteration's diff value as a number'. The verify mechanism is the log-line value; 'honoured' names the contract, the log line does the binary work. Cited principle: PRD Phase 1 scope item 15 — 'verify steps live in SKILL.md, not in the AC contract.' The same separation applies to tasks: the acceptance describes the contract; the SKILL.md verify step (T7 Scope line: 'threshold read from `admin/config.json.design.diffThreshold`') describes the mechanism.
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: none — push back; T7 acceptance retained as-is. The threshold-override sub-clause is binary against the existing diff-value-as-number rule.

goal-r1-f2.rationale: AC-7 has two binary halves and T8 only verifies one. Adding a binary check for the diff-visualisation path closes the gap and matches the pattern T9 uses for citation-format checks (the artefact path resolves to a real file).

The path resolves to a non-empty PNG file. A run with an empty path or unwritten file is a failed run.'

Gate 2's simplicity-r1-f1 already established that R6 and R10 are separate single-concern requirements (interview Round 5's 'but add' phrasing — see debate-log/prd-gate2/findings/round-3/simplicity-reviewer.json line 10). The same 1:1 R→T trace clarity argument applies at the task level: merging T10 into T6 would create a multi-anchor task (T6 covering both R6 and R10) and lose the visual coverage matrix's symmetry. AC-5 already verifies both rules — the 'shared AC' argument the reviewer cites is symmetric, not asymmetric: AC-5's coverage-by-two-tasks is the same surface as the requirements-by-two-rules structure. Cited evidence: features/001-design-skill/001-design-skill-prd.md R6 line 65 ('--default-when-missing opt-in flag') and R10 line 81 ('INVENTED VALUES sub-block') — two requirements in the PRD; Gate 2 closing decision lines 73-74 ('R10's separation from R6 is load-bearing... two distinct decisions').
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: none — push back; T6 and T10 retained as separate tasks. R10 stays mapped to T10 in the coverage matrix.
